questions.text: When working on a group project, you naturally tend to:

options.text: Take the lead and organize tasks
Support others and keep the team motivated
Focus on details and quality of work
Generate ideas and think outside the box

questions.text: Which of these excites you the most?

options.text: Solving a tricky math or logic puzzle
Creating something artistic (drawing, writing, music)
Helping a friend solve a personal problem
Organizing an event or activity

questions.text: What kind of recognition matters most to you?

options.text: Academic excellence/top marks
Being known as creative/talented
Being seen as helpful/dependable
Being seen as a leader/organizer

questions.text: If you had a free day with no obligations, you'd most likely:

options.text: Read, study, or learn something new
Work on a creative hobby
Spend time with friends/family
Plan or organize something (an event, a trip, a project)

questions.text: When faced with a new challenge, you usually:

options.text: Plan carefully before acting
Jump in and learn as you go
Ask others for advice first
Research thoroughly before deciding

questions.text: What kind of subjects do you enjoy most in school?

options.text: Maths/Physics (logic, numbers)
Biology/Chemistry (life sciences)
Languages/Social Studies (people, communication)
Computers/Arts (creativity, design)

questions.text: How do you usually react under pressure (exams, deadlines)?

options.text: I stay calm and work through it systematically
I get anxious but push through anyway
I seek help/support from others
I thrive — pressure motivates me

questions.text: Imagine your ideal study or work day. Which description comes closest?

options.text: A fixed schedule where I know exactly what happens and when
A planned day with some room to move things around
A loose outline that I adjust as the day unfolds
An open day where I decide what to do as I go

questions.text: After a full day of group activities — classes, team practice, events — how do you usually feel?

options.text: Energised — I would happily continue with more people time
Positive — I enjoy people, balanced with some quiet time
A little tired — I need some quiet time before doing more
Drained — I recharge best completely on my own

questions.text: Suppose you had two career options — one secure and predictable, the other uncertain but with a much bigger upside. Which way would you lean?

options.text: I would take the bold option — a big opportunity is worth the uncertainty
I would take a calculated chance after weighing what could go wrong
I would lean towards the secure option unless the upside was very convincing
I would choose the secure path — stability matters most to me

questions.text: Think about the work you are most proud of. How was it usually done?

options.text: Alone, from start to finish
Mostly alone, checking in with others at key points
Shared with one or two close partners
Within a full team where everyone contributed throughout

questions.text: A long-term project has no fixed deadline. What actually happens?

options.text: I set my own milestones and start well before I need to
I make a clear plan first, then work through it steadily
I get moving once a reminder or a date appears on the horizon
I do my best work only when the pressure is truly on

questions.text: After 12th, which stream/path excites you most?

options.text: Engineering/Technology
Medicine/Healthcare
Commerce/Business/Finance
Arts/Design/Humanities
Not sure yet

questions.text: If you had to pick a career today, what matters most to you?

options.text: High earning potential
Job stability/security
Creative freedom
Making a social impact

questions.text: Do you see yourself as someone who prefers:

options.text: Working with numbers and data
Working with people directly
Working with technology and machines
Working with ideas and creativity

questions.text: How much real-world exploration have you done of the career you are considering?

options.text: I have spoken to people working in the field or attended related programmes
I have researched courses, colleges, and career paths on my own
I have mainly discussed it with family, friends, or teachers
I have not really begun exploring yet

questions.text: How aligned are you and your family on your career direction?

options.text: We agree — my family supports the path I want
We see it differently, but we are discussing it openly
My family has a set path in mind that I am expected to follow
We have not seriously discussed it yet

questions.text: Where do you currently stand on competitive entrance exams such as JEE, NEET, or CLAT?

options.text: I have started preparing and have a clear target exam
I intend to attempt one but have not started preparing yet
I am unsure whether these exams are the right route for me
My intended path does not require these exams

questions.text: Looking ten to fifteen years ahead, which of these comes closest to your long-term dream?

options.text: Becoming a recognised expert in a specialised professional field
Building and leading a successful business of my own
Serving people through medicine, law, or public service
Creating original work in design, media, or the arts

gating_question.text: Looking beyond Class 12, which path do you currently see for yourself?

options.text: I plan to study further — a degree or professional course, in India or abroad
I plan to start working or join my family's business
I have not decided yet

on_end_test.report_instruction: Generate final report using only personality, career_specific, and work_environment sections. Do NOT include any abroad-related section, scoring, or content in the report.

questions.text: Have you thought about where you would like to pursue your higher education?

options.text: I am definitely interested in studying abroad
I am open to studying abroad, but I have not decided
I would prefer to study in India

questions.text: If you did study abroad, what would matter most in choosing where to go?

options.text: Quality of education and university reputation
Affordability — tuition costs and scholarship availability
Post-study work rights and long-term settlement options
International exposure, culture, and life experience

questions.text: Which study destinations are on your mind, even loosely? Select all that apply.

options.text: USA
UK
Canada
Australia
Germany
Other/Not decided

questions.text: When would you realistically want to begin studying abroad?

options.text: Within the next 12 months
In 1 to 2 years — right after Class 12
In 2 to 3 years — possibly after starting a degree in India
No fixed timeline yet — still exploring

questions.text: How would your education abroad most likely be funded?

options.text: Fully family-funded — finances are already planned
Part family funding, part scholarship or education loan
Mainly dependent on scholarships or education loans
Budget not yet discussed with family
